title: Word: Edit with Copilot for users in Microsoft 365 GCC
summary: The briefing accurately reports the disagreement between the roadmap and Microsoft's government-cloud availability table, and supports its licensing and data-boundary statements. The licence and Anthropic controls are documented; their abbreviated navigation paths need minor clarification.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rendered controls table
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses reaches licence assignment; the prose also abbreviates the route to Billing > Licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page. Select a product. On the product details page, select Assign licenses.
claims.fix: Keep controls[0].ui unchanged. Replace '(Billing > Licenses)' in Risk assessment with '(Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses; to remove access, select the user or group and Unassign licenses)', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/assign-licenses-to-users.

claims.where: controls[0].api; rendered controls table
claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope: Roles; Governance controls
claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least a License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: PowerShell licence assignment can use the User.ReadWrite.All permission scope.
claims.quote: Assigning and removing licenses for a user requires the User.ReadWrite.All permission scope or one of the other permissions listed in the 'Assign license' Microsoft Graph API reference page.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: A user needs a UsageLocation before a licence can be assigned through the PowerShell route.
claims.quote: You can only assign licenses to user accounts that have the UsageLocation property set to a valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Claude models and their admin option are unavailable to federal GCC customers and all GCC High and DoD customers.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The Anthropic setting became available for non-federal GCC customers on 22 July 2026.
claims.quote: As of July 22, 2026, a new setting is available in the Microsoft 365 admin center that allows non-federal customers in Government Community Cloud (GCC) to use Anthropic models.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; rendered controls table
claims.claim: The printed Anthropic route follows the GCC-specific page through the terms acknowledgement and user-access section.
claims.quote: Review the information in the Terms and conditions section, and if they're acceptable, select the I acknowledge and agree to the above terms checkbox. Under Choose which users can access Anthropic models, select All users, or specify users and groups, and then select Save.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].ui.path and the rendered route to 'Copilot > Settings > View all > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Available subprocessors for your organization > Anthropic > Terms and conditions > I acknowledge and agree to the above terms > Choose which users can access Anthropic models > All users or users and groups', matching https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/anthropic-non-federal-gcc.
